blocks.text: Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) then named five other Sahabah (RA) and stated that the five of them together with himself went into the eye socket of the creature and none was even able to see them until they emerged. They then took a rib of the creature and stood it up like a bow. Thereafter, they selected the tallest person sitting upon the largest camel and the biggest carriage and the man was able to pass beneath the rib without even lowering his head.[^1]

Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) also reports, "Rasulullaah ﷺ once dispatched a regiment of three hundred men under the command of Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA). I was amongst the men and we were sent to a coastal area. We were still travelling when our provisions came to an end. Abu Ubaydah (RA) instructed us to gather together all that was left of the provisions and when it was done, it amounted to only two satchels of dates. He rationed it to us little by little until it was almost finished and we then received only a single date each (for the day)."
"Of what use was a single date," one of the narrators asked Hadhrat Jaabir (RA). Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) replied, "When the rations were finished, we missed even that single date." Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) then continued the story saying, "We then reached the sea shore, where we were surprised to see a fish (lying on the ground which was) the size of a hill. The army then ate from this fish for eighteen days. Abu Ubaydah (RA) then had two of the ribs placed upright, had a carriage strapped to a camel and then passed the camel and carriage beneath the ribs. The camel passed through without touching the ribs."[^2]

In another narration, Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) states, "Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched three hundred of us under the command of Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) to ambush one of the Quraysh's caravans. (When our provisions ran out) We started to suffer such extreme hunger that we resorted to eating leaves. It was for this reason that this army was known as the Army of Leaves. Someone then slaughtered three camels (to feed the army), after which he slaughtered another three and then another three until Abu Ubaydah (RA) stopped him (because it was depriving them of transport). It was then that the sea threw out a fish called Ambar, from which we ate for half a month and from which we even derived oil. This eventually restored our strength..." The narration then goes on to mention the incident of the fish's ribs.[^3]

In yet another narration, Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) says, "Rasulullaah ﷺ dispatched us under the command of Abu Ubaydah bin Jarraah (RA) to intercept a caravan belonging to the Quraysh. Rasulullaah ﷺ gave us a bag of dates as the journey's provisions because he had nothing else to give us. Abu Ubaydah (RA) would therefore give us a daily ration of one date each."
